newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX edges up to yr-high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips mixed, SAX edges up to yr-high.

text.p: Major Slovak stocks closed mixed in moderate trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, as the 16-share official SAX index edged up 0.02 points to a year-high of 206.00.

Steel maker VSZ led the day's trading in terms of volume, closing down two crowns at 728 with 13,704 shares changing hands, but gains to broader shares of Slovakofarma, builder Vahostav and insurer Slovensksa Poistovna helped boost the index.

Brokers said they expected the market to extend its uptrend slightly over the week, boosted by continuing foreign demand for what they say are still undervalued stocks. The SAX index has risen 18.4 percent since the beginning of this year.
"We should not see any radical moves of the index this week, though demand for blue chips could push the market a bit higher," said Libor Briska of Creditanstalt.
Brokers said most of the block of VSZ shares appeared to have been an agreed deal settled through the BSE.
"But you can trade VSZ at current levels so the price seems to reflect the real market value of the stock," Briska said.

Oil refiner Slovnaft fell 10 crowns to land at its nominal value of 1,000 crowns but brokers said it remains one of the few liquid shares that continues to attract foreign interest. They said they expect its price to hover around current levels in the near future.
Overall volume fell to 364,041 shares, from 453,510 stocks traded on Friday, while turnover rose to 338.90 million crowns, from 297.34 million.
